fixes.explanation: Yep, that's what the Teacher saw: "A righteous man perishing in his righteousness…" (Ecclesiastes 7:15) He says it right out loud, in the middle of calling his life futile. Sometimes the Bible just tells you the hard part plainly.

That's it. "Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?" (Ecclesiastes 7:16) The Teacher is asking a real question there. He's warning about going too far, and I'll be honest, I read that and my hat tilted a little.
Yes, baker, yes! "For he who fears God will follow both warnings." (Ecclesiastes 7:18) The Teacher puts it right there at the end of the verse. Fearing God is where he lands.

That's right. "Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins." (Ecclesiastes 7:20) The Teacher says it about everybody. And yes, that includes the guy who shows up with the perfect batch of cookies, which is me, and I'm sitting in that boat with you.
I wish, friend! A thank you would've been lovely. The Teacher says, "…or you may hear your servant cursing you." (Ecclesiastes 7:21) That's why he says not to pay attention to every word.

Yes, that's how he says it. "All this I tested by wisdom, saying, 'I resolve to be wise.' But it was beyond me." (Ecclesiastes 7:23) He tested all this by wisdom, and wisdom still outran him. I think that's a humble thing to admit.

That's right. "What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?" (Ecclesiastes 7:24) Picture reaching down a well and your arm just runs out. That's the feeling the Teacher is putting into words, and he asks the question out loud.
You got it. "The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared." (Ecclesiastes 7:26) The Teacher puts two men side by side. The one who pleases God is the one who gets away.

That's the word. "While my soul was still searching but not finding…" (Ecclesiastes 7:28) He kept looking even when he wasn't finding. I know a little about waiting around for something to turn up, after all those years in the back of a junk drawer.
Not yet, friend. The Teacher says, "While my soul was still searching but not finding…" (Ecclesiastes 7:28) He's still looking at that point. No confetti yet.

The text doesn't say tired, friend. The Teacher says, "…God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes." (Ecclesiastes 7:29) Nobody got worn out. They went looking for schemes, and plenty of them.
